summary.oneLiner: INOX India delivered strong Q1FY26 growth with 16.7% revenue rise, driven by breakthrough orders in ultra-high-purity ammonia containers and India’s first CO2 battery storage system, while LNG and keg segments show scalable momentum; the company’s diversified high-margin product portfolio and strategic capex expansion position it to capture India’s clean energy transition and global industrial supply chain reshoring.
summary.business: INOX India Ltd (INOXCVA) designs, engineers, manufactures, delivers and installs vacuum-insulated cryogenic equipment and systems for the storage, distribution and transfer of cryogens (helium, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, LNG and more) across a temperature range of 2-200 Kelvin. The Company operates through four divisions - Industrial Gas, LNG, Cryo Scientific and Stainless Steel Kegs - serving 590+ customers spanning industrial gas producers, LNG operators, space agencies, healthcare institutions and beverage companies across more than 100 countries.

Industrial Gas Division: Cryogenic storage tanks (1 litre portable dewars to 1,500,000 litre stationary tanks)
LNG Division: Static LNG tanks (up to one million litres)
Cryo Scientific Division (CSD): ITER fusion project components (cryolines, Vacuum Vessel Thermal Shield repair)
Stainless Steel KEG Division: Premium returnable stainless steel beverage kegs (in collaboration with Supermonte Group, Italy)

currentContext.strengths: Global leader in customised cryogenic equipment; among the largest cryogenic tank manufacturers in the world|Complete end-to-end capability: design, engineering, manufacturing, installation and after-sales service|Diversified customer base of 590+ clients across industrial gas, LNG, scientific and beverage segments|Export-oriented manufacturing at Kandla Special Economic Zone providing logistics and duty advantages for international business|International commercial infrastructure: subsidiaries and service centres in Brazil, marketing offices in Europe|Backward and forward integration with group companies contributing 10% of revenues|Robust financial profile: Debt-Equity of 0.06x (FY26), interest coverage of 38.04x, RONW of 23.08%
currentContext.strategies: Establishing global leadership in modular mini-LNG terminal technology, having delivered projects in Scotland and Antigua and now executing a third major contract in The Bahamas as a regional clean energy hub|Building capabilities in small-scale LNG (SS-LNG) projects for remote industrial locations, island nations and off-grid power generation, and executing projects across multiple geographies|Continuing to build opportunities in emerging segments such as hydrogen storage, long-duration energy storage and advanced cryogenic applications aligned with the clean energy transition|Positioning as a critical enabler of India's hydrogen economy under the National Green Hydrogen Mission through liquid hydrogen cryogenic tanks, transfer systems and distribution infrastructure|Extending addressable market into stainless steel beverage kegs (division launched FY25) in collaboration with Supermonte Group, Italy, targeting global beverage producers phasing out single-use containers|Expanding global engagement through participation in international industry forums and customer collaborations in LNG infrastructure, marine fuel systems and small-scale LNG applications|Deepening presence in emerging cryogenic applications - hydrogen storage, semiconductor-grade ultra-high-purity gas equipment, and CO2/liquid air energy storage systems|Dividend of Rs 2/- per equity share of Rs 2/- face value (100%), as recommended by the Board, to be declared at the 49th AGM (23rd June 2026) and paid out of the Company's profits.
currentContext.expansion: Targeted investments in advanced automation and precision fabrication strengthened manufacturing capabilities during FY26, enhancing throughput and ensuring adherence to global quality standards, positioning the Company's facilities as competitive export hubs for complex, high-value infrastructure. The Kandla (KASEZ) export-oriented facility was honoured with the Award for Excellence in Export 2024-25. Capital expenditure allocated toward enhancement of sustainability and safety measures represented 5.65% of total capex in FY26 (6.29% in FY25), per BRSR Principle 2 disclosure.

risks.note: Top 10 customers contributed 51% of FY26 revenues, creating sensitivity to individual customer demand cycles.

Export revenues comprised 59% of FY26 revenues, exposing the Company to anti-dumping investigations, trade barriers, shipping disruptions and currency volatility in key export markets, as well as trade-policy shifts.

Dependence on four principal manufacturing facilities in India; disruption at a facility could affect production, mitigated by preventive maintenance, business continuity planning and multi-plant redundancy.
Exposure to steel, stainless steel and energy price fluctuations; mitigated by strategic procurement, vendor diversification and selective pass-through pricing in contracts.
Orders are subject to revision, delay or cancellation, which could affect revenue visibility from the order backlog.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality from long equipment life cycles
risks.note: Major operators periodically relocate existing equipment rather than buy new, deferring procurement and creating episodic demand troughs.

risks.risk: Commodity price and policy sensitivity of LNG/hydrogen demand
risks.note: Future demand for LNG and hydrogen equipment is sensitive to commodity prices and government policy continuity (e.g. India's gas-in-energy-mix and Green Hydrogen Mission targets), both of which carry structural uncertainty.
Increasing competition from low-cost manufacturers in emerging markets offering aggressive pricing on standardised equipment categories.

one-line thesis: INOX India delivered strong Q1FY26 growth with 16.7% revenue rise, driven by breakthrough orders in ultra-high-purity ammonia containers and India’s first CO2 battery storage system, while LNG and keg segments show scalable momentum; the company’s diversified high-margin product portfolio and strategic capex expansion position it to capture India’s clean energy transition and global industrial supply chain reshoring.
financial scorecard: revenue: +16.7% YoY; EBITDA/margin: +19.4% YoY, margin improved from 23.1% to 25.3% (excludes one-off other income of INR12.5cr from reversal of prior provisions); PAT (rptd): +18.9% YoY; PAT (normalized): +15.2% YoY (excluding INR12.5cr other income); order book: INR1,457cr as of Jun 30, 2025 (45% IG, 32% LNG, 23% Cryo); net debt: INR275cr fund availability (net cash position)
guidance: revenue growth: 18-20% YoY; margin: stable EBITDA margin target of ~25%; order inflow: expects strong Q2-Q4 inflow from LNG, Cryo, and keg segments; capex/commissioning: INR80cr total capex for FY26, including INR5-6cr for LNG tank capacity expansion at Kalol, Savli plant stabilization by Q4FY26
order book & pipeline: INR1,457cr as of Jun 30, 2025; 63% export content; major components: INR145cr ITER Cryostat Thermal Shield order (2-year duration), 11 ultra-high-purity ammonia containers (2 delivered, 9 in production), 145 LNG fuel tanks dispatched, 28,000cr keg orders received in Q2FY26 (pre-announced)
segment / subsidiary detail: Industrial Gas: 48% of revenue; led by ultra-high-purity ammonia containers (first in India, 11 units ordered) and CO2 battery storage (first order, 26 units); LNG: 29% of revenue; 145 tanks dispatched, capacity expansion to 5,000-6,000 tanks/year by end-FY26; Cryo Scientific: 19% of revenue; INR145cr ITER order (90% in-house fabrication); Beverage Kegs: low base but accelerating; 6.4cr Q1 orders, Q2 FY26 orders at INR28,000cr (pre-announced), global approvals from Heineken & AB InBev secured, Asahi/Carlsberg audits scheduled for Sep-Oct 2025
growth verticals / optionality: LNG fueling station ecosystem (Adani/Ambani land conversion policy), SMR nuclear reactor manufacturing (bidding with govt partners), hydrogen equipment scaling, CO2 battery commercialization (global replication potential), keg volume ramp-up (3-4x current size target by FY28)
margins & cost dynamics: Higher margins in new products: ultra-purity ammonia and CO2 battery storage (premium pricing); cost pressures mitigated by antidumping duties on Chinese kegs; Savli plant costs front-loaded (stabilizing by Q4FY26); steel tariff impact on US cylinders limited to material cost only (50% of price), EBIT margin remains 14-15%
capex / expansion: INR80cr total for FY26; INR5-6cr for LNG tank capacity expansion at Kalol; capex for Kandla (1,500m³ vessels) and Savli plant upgrades; no new greenfield announced yet, scaling via brownfield expansion
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for LNG and keg capacity; maintaining net cash position (INR275cr available); no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on organic growth and strategic order execution
risks & watch-items: Keg volume ramp-up delayed vs internal targets; LNG station rollout slower than policy potential; execution risk on ITER project (long duration); global trade policy shifts (US tariffs); competitive pressure from Chinese players in kegs (mitigated by antidumping duties)
management quality / tone: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized technological leadership, global approvals, and policy tailwinds; tone on LNG and kegs is bullish; ITER and CO2 battery framed as strategic differentiators, not one-offs
non-obvious takeaways: The INR28,000cr Q2FY26 keg order (pre-announced) is likely a cumulative pipeline value, not a single order — indicating strong pre-commitments from global brewers; ITER’s 200 CTS panels represent a multi-year, high-margin, repeatable workstream beyond the INR145cr order; CO2 battery order from Italy signals export-ready clean energy tech, not just domestic

JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
